FINAL OUTPUT CONTRACT: your ENTIRE final message must be exactly one bare JSON object (schema_version "1") - no code fence, no text before or after it. The Markdown answer lives only inside its reply_markdown string; each defect goes in findings[]. A prose final message cannot be ingested, however good the answer is.

Read the brief at `.collab/companions-2026-09-26/handoffs/40-claude-wave28b-acceptance.md` (path relative to the repository root, which is your working directory) and answer every numbered question in it.

Review range: `1de388e..e5c6992` - the range changes 43 files, 9583 lines (8924 insertions, 659 deletions; git diff --shortstat). Plan your reading for its size.

Tools: you may read files of the repository (read_file); writing files, the shell and the web tools are disabled in this consultation (--disable-write --disable-shell --disable-web-tools) - do not try them; make NO file changes; a check that needs a command belongs under `## Requested checks`.

Review purpose: acceptance. Decide whether the result can be accepted. The verdict, the blockers, the unproven scenarios and an OBSERVABLE first-run checklist (what must be seen in logs or output on the first real run before an exit code 0 is believed) are mandatory.

Findings from earlier consultations in this task that are still open (id - status - locations - claim - trigger - verify):

10|## Telemetry: what leaves the machine
11|
12|D1. A closed vocabulary instead of operator text (F36-1 major). The roster label and the model name are text the
13|    operator typed. The event carries `provider` = the vendor class derived from the ENDPOINT host through a
14|    table shipped with the bridge (`api.openai.com` and the ChatGPT login -> `openai`, `api.z.ai` -> `zai`, and
15|    so on for every provider the README documents; the engines agy and muse -> `google`, `meta`), anything else
16|    -> `other`; `model` = the model name only when the vendor class is known AND the name matches that
17|    vendor's published pattern in the same table, else `other`. `tags` carry the same two values. The label
18|    never leaves the machine. The allowlist test of the harness walks the VALUES too: a roster with a label
19|    and a model that look like a company name must produce `other` / `other`.
20|D2. The sender has a deadline (F36-2 major). One flush ends after 60 s in all, whatever the intake does; one
21|    request is bounded as a whole (connect, send, read) by 8 s; the flush lock is released in `finally` and a
22|    lock older than 5 minutes is taken over; what is not sent stays in the spool.
23|D3. The sender starts with a minimal environment (F36-3 major): an ALLOW list, not a scrub list - the system
24|    variables a PowerShell process needs (SystemRoot, windir, ComSpec, PATH, PATHEXT, TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE,
25|    HOME, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, ProgramData, ProgramFiles*, PSModulePath, the locale and proxy variables),
26|    `CODEX_HOME`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL`, and in a harness the test mode
27|    variables. No provider key, no host marker, no other `CODEX_CONSULT_*` variable.
28|D4. The intake URL (F36-9, F37-4): `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` stays an operator setting and must be https;
29|    plain http is accepted only for a loopback address AND with `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1`.
30|D5. The salt is created atomically (F36-9): write a temporary file, move it without overwriting; a creator
31|    that loses reads the winner's salt; never delete a salt that parses.
32|D6. A spool that cannot be written is visible (F35-1, F36-8, F37-6): the append waits up to 5 s; a failure
33|    puts `telemetry event not spooled (<why>)` into `warnings[]` of the ledger entry and onto the console, and
34|    `-Status` counts the events not spooled since the last flush.
35|D7. `-Complain` keeps its promise (F36-7, F37-5): the spool keeps the exact bytes that were shown; the deferred
36|    send posts those bytes.
37|D8. The sender against the intake as it is built: a batch refused with 400 `events[i]: reason` - drop event i
38|    (one line in `.last`), resend the rest, at most three times per flush; 413 - halve the batch; 403 - stop
39|    the flush, keep the spool, say why; any other 4xx - keep the spool, say why.

41|    id>?public_ref=<ref>`; `-Forget -Local` removes the local spool and the salt. The README says the intake is
42|    live and names both.

45|

47|     `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_*` are removed from the environment of ENGINE children and of the sender (a panel
48|     member, which is the bridge itself, keeps them); a run that finds `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` prints `test
49|     mode is ON: test hooks are honoured` on the console and puts it into `warnings[]` - every harness expects
50|     that line.
51|D11. The host hint by path is anchored (F36-4 major): the root of the running script is compared with the
52|     plugin directories of the hosts resolved from the home directory (`<home>/.claude/plugins/cache/`,
53|     `<home>/.codex/plugins/cache/` or `<codex home>/plugins/cache/`, `<home>/.zcode/cli/plugins/cache/`,
54|     `<home>/.qwen/extensions/`); a path that merely contains such a name gives no hint.
55|D12. An open tool call and the stall cut (F36-11, F32-7): the suspension ends after 2 x stall seconds without
56|     any growth of the stream (no floor of 1800 s); the cut names the open tool call.
57|D13. The health update survives a crash (F36-6, F37-1): inside the lock the run appends the record to a
58|     journal beside the health file (a local append, no lock wait); the retry after the lock, or the next run
59|     of any repository, applies the journal and empties it; the warning says `a retry follows the commit`,
60|     and the detached status record and the console summary carry the outcome of the retry.
61|D14. The confirmed kill (F37-2, F37-3): a descendant counts as alive only with its start time unchanged; on a
62|     host that is not Windows and has no `pgrep` the children are read from `ps -o pid=,ppid=`, then `/proc`;
63|     only when nothing works is the kill unconfirmed.
64|D15. The window of the reviewer reaches the engine (seen live: the k3 member failed with 401 in the middle of
65|     its review): a roster entry with `context_tokens` gives codex `-c model_context_window=<n>` and `-c
66|     model_auto_compact_token_limit=<0.8 n>`; the ledger records both; for agy and muse the README says the
67|     key guards only the start.
68|D16. Days are local (reported by the other implementation after a run across midnight): every place that
69|     computes a day (the rollout search, the spool file name, the health file) uses the LOCAL date, as the
70|     engine does; one harness row crosses midnight.

73|
74|D17. Host instructions (F36-10): every command block of a host section uses ONE name for the plugin directory
75|     and defines it in the same block; the hook block works when copied as written on every host.
76|D18. The waiting section (F36-10): the text says which price is a full wake and which a cache read, and a
77|     compaction after the cache expired costs a cold resume PLUS the summary.
78|D19. Harnesses report and go on: `harness-pending` section (e) and `harness-fixes` F04-11 print FAIL with what
79|     was missing instead of stopping with an exception. `harness-pending` (e) injects the registration failure

11|
12|D1. A closed vocabulary instead of operator text (F36-1 major). The roster label and the model name are text the
13|    operator typed. The event carries `provider` = the vendor class derived from the ENDPOINT host through a
14|    table shipped with the bridge (`api.openai.com` and the ChatGPT login -> `openai`, `api.z.ai` -> `zai`, and
15|    so on for every provider the README documents; the engines agy and muse -> `google`, `meta`), anything else
16|    -> `other`; `model` = the model name only when the vendor class is known AND the name matches that
17|    vendor's published pattern in the same table, else `other`. `tags` carry the same two values. The label
18|    never leaves the machine. The allowlist test of the harness walks the VALUES too: a roster with a label
19|    and a model that look like a company name must produce `other` / `other`.
20|D2. The sender has a deadline (F36-2 major). One flush ends after 60 s in all, whatever the intake does; one
21|    request is bounded as a whole (connect, send, read) by 8 s; the flush lock is released in `finally` and a
22|    lock older than 5 minutes is taken over; what is not sent stays in the spool.
23|D3. The sender starts with a minimal environment (F36-3 major): an ALLOW list, not a scrub list - the system
24|    variables a PowerShell process needs (SystemRoot, windir, ComSpec, PATH, PATHEXT, TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE,
25|    HOME, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, ProgramData, ProgramFiles*, PSModulePath, the locale and proxy variables),
26|    `CODEX_HOME`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY`, `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL`, and in a harness the test mode
27|    variables. No provider key, no host marker, no other `CODEX_CONSULT_*` variable.
28|D4. The intake URL (F36-9, F37-4): `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` stays an operator setting and must be https;
29|    plain http is accepted only for a loopback address AND with `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1`.
30|D5. The salt is created atomically (F36-9): write a temporary file, move it without overwriting; a creator
31|    that loses reads the winner's salt; never delete a salt that parses.
32|D6. A spool that cannot be written is visible (F35-1, F36-8, F37-6): the append waits up to 5 s; a failure
33|    puts `telemetry event not spooled (<why>)` into `warnings[]` of the ledger entry and onto the console, and
34|    `-Status` counts the events not spooled since the last flush.
35|D7. `-Complain` keeps its promise (F36-7, F37-5): the spool keeps the exact bytes that were shown; the deferred
36|    send posts those bytes.
37|D8. The sender against the intake as it is built: a batch refused with 400 `events[i]: reason` - drop event i
38|    (one line in `.last`), resend the rest, at most three times per flush; 413 - halve the batch; 403 - stop
39|    the flush, keep the spool, say why; any other 4xx - keep the spool, say why.
40|D9. Delete my data: `codex-telemetry.ps1 -Forget -PublicRef <ref>` sends `DELETE /T/v2/instances/<instance
41|    id>?public_ref=<ref>`; `-Forget -Local` removes the local spool and the salt. The README says the intake is
42|    live and names both.
43|
44|## Test mode, host hint, member control
45|
46|D10. Test mode cannot leak or stay unnoticed (F36-5 major): `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE` and every
47|     `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_*` are removed from the environment of ENGINE children and of the sender (a panel
48|     member, which is the bridge itself, keeps them); a run that finds `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` prints `test
49|     mode is ON: test hooks are honoured` on the console and puts it into `warnings[]` - every harness expects
50|     that line.
51|D11. The host hint by path is anchored (F36-4 major): the root of the running script is compared with the
52|     plugin directories of the hosts resolved from the home directory (`<home>/.claude/plugins/cache/`,
53|     `<home>/.codex/plugins/cache/` or `<codex home>/plugins/cache/`, `<home>/.zcode/cli/plugins/cache/`,
54|     `<home>/.qwen/extensions/`); a path that merely contains such a name gives no hint.
55|D12. An open tool call and the stall cut (F36-11, F32-7): the suspension ends after 2 x stall seconds without
56|     any growth of the stream (no floor of 1800 s); the cut names the open tool call.
57|D13. The health update survives a crash (F36-6, F37-1): inside the lock the run appends the record to a
58|     journal beside the health file (a local append, no lock wait); the retry after the lock, or the next run
59|     of any repository, applies the journal and empties it; the warning says `a retry follows the commit`,
60|     and the detached status record and the console summary carry the outcome of the retry.
61|D14. The confirmed kill (F37-2, F37-3): a descendant counts as alive only with its start time unchanged; on a
62|     host that is not Windows and has no `pgrep` the children are read from `ps -o pid=,ppid=`, then `/proc`;
63|     only when nothing works is the kill unconfirmed.
64|D15. The window of the reviewer reaches the engine (seen live: the k3 member failed with 401 in the middle of
65|     its review): a roster entry with `context_tokens` gives codex `-c model_context_window=<n>` and `-c
66|     model_auto_compact_token_limit=<0.8 n>`; the ledger records both; for agy and muse the README says the
67|     key guards only the start.
68|D16. Days are local (reported by the other implementation after a run across midnight): every place that
69|     computes a day (the rollout search, the spool file name, the health file) uses the LOCAL date, as the
70|     engine does; one harness row crosses midnight.
71|
72|## Documentation and harnesses
73|
74|D17. Host instructions (F36-10): every command block of a host section uses ONE name for the plugin directory
75|     and defines it in the same block; the hook block works when copied as written on every host.
76|D18. The waiting section (F36-10): the text says which price is a full wake and which a cache read, and a
77|     compaction after the cache expired costs a cold resume PLUS the summary.
78|D19. Harnesses report and go on: `harness-pending` section (e) and `harness-fixes` F04-11 print FAIL with what
79|     was missing instead of stopping with an exception. `harness-pending` (e) injects the registration failure
80|     through the hook `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_REGISTER_FAIL` (gated by test mode), not by patching a function, so
81|     the rows measure any implementation given with `-ScriptsDir`.
82|
83|Candidates recorded in the ROADMAP, not in this wave: R21, R22 (reviewer children without the plugin of the
84|coordinator and without multi-agent tools), R23.
85|Re-acceptance: by mimo (required) with glm; the brief lists D1-D19 and the commit.
